canonical.title: Athens to the islands, summer 2026: ferries, ports and when to fly instead

parent.title: A routed one-week Greece plan from an Athens arrival, summer 2026

siblings.title: Athens non-negotiables: the summer 2026 field manual
siblings.summary: Book the 08:00 Acropolis slot, pair it with the Acropolis Museum and the Ancient Agora, and treat almost everything else in Athens as optional — with 2026 prices, the heat-closure rule and the sites that are shut this summer.

siblings.title: After Athens: Greek island clusters compared for a 3-5 day August 2026 tail
siblings.summary: For a 3-5 day tail after Athens in August 2026, one Cyclades island (Naxos or Milos) beats any two-island hop; the Saronic is the only cluster where two islands in four days is not a trap.

siblings.title: Day trips from Athens without changing base — summer 2026
siblings.summary: One spare day in August: take the early hydrofoil to Hydra, or Delphi if you want antiquity — and skip Meteora and the three-island cruise entirely.

siblings.title: The mainland tail: a Peloponnese loop and/or Meteora after Athens
siblings.summary: A car-based Peloponnese loop plus Meteora is cheaper and emptier than the Cyclades in August but far hotter and more driving — here's the routed 5-night tail that works.

siblings.title: Eating and Drinking in Athens and the Islands, Summer 2026
siblings.summary: Route Athens around souvlaki row, one mezedopoleio dinner and one rooftop; skip the starred night unless you want it — and put Sifnos or Naxos on the ferry list.

sources.title: Athens ferry ports compared: Piraeus, Rafina or Lavrio
sources.claim: Piraeus, Rafina and Lavrio serve different island groups, and each needs a different minimum connection buffer after an international flight.

sources.title: Ports of Athens — Athens by Locals
sources.claim: Transfer times and costs from Athens airport and central Athens to Piraeus, Rafina and Lavrio.

sources.title: Blue Star Ferries — Piraeus port map
sources.claim: Piraeus assigns departures to numbered gates E1-E9 by destination and vessel.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — ferries from Piraeus
sources.claim: 2026 durations, frequencies and starting fares for the main routes out of Piraeus.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — Rafina to Mykonos
sources.claim: Rafina-Mykonos runs up to 10 times daily in summer, 2h05-4h40, from €35.50.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — Greek island ferry schedules 2026
sources.claim: 2026 Rafina route fares to Andros, Tinos and Mykonos.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — Greek ferries
sources.claim: High-speed catamarans cost roughly double a conventional car ferry, and SeaJets seats, cabins and car spots sell out in July-August.

sources.title: Go-Ferry — Greek ferries trends and insights
sources.claim: For the July 15-September 15 peak, book 2-3 months ahead, and 3-4 months for August cabins and vehicles.

sources.title: Greece Trips — when a ferry is cancelled
sources.claim: EU Regulation 1177/2010 entitles you to a refund within seven days or free re-routing when a ferry is cancelled.

sources.title: Dave's Travel Pages — the meltemi winds
sources.claim: The meltemi blows June-September, peaks in July-August at 7-8 Beaufort and affects high-speed ferries more.

sources.title: Taxi to Athens — airport to Piraeus port
sources.claim: Airport to Piraeus by taxi is metered (€50-58 day) not the €40 flat fare.

sources.title: X96 timetable — Athens airport to Piraeus port
sources.claim: The X96 express runs 24 hours from arrivals between Exits 4 and 5, every 30-40 minutes.

sources.title: MyArtemida — airport to Rafina bus timetable
sources.claim: KTEL Attikis runs the airport-Rafina bus roughly hourly from Exits 2 and 3, ~30 minutes, €4-5.50 cash.

sources.title: Ferries Greece — Blue Star ticket collection
sources.claim: Paper tickets can be collected at the port office with the reservation code up to one hour before departure.

sources.title: Blue Star Ferries — online booking and web check-in
sources.claim: Web check-in opens 48 hours and closes 2 hours before departure and issues a QR e-ticket.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — renting a car in Greece
sources.claim: Taking a rental car on a Greek ferry needs the rental company's permission; island one-way drop-offs are rarely allowed.

sources.title: Kos Car Hire — taking rental cars on a ferry
sources.claim: Ferry permission must be in writing, costs roughly €30-74, and standard insurance may lapse at sea.

sources.title: Wego — Athens to Santorini
sources.claim: Piraeus-Santorini is 4h50-5h35 by SeaJets from ~€79.70 versus 7h30-8h on Blue Star from ~€46.50.

sources.title: Aegean Airlines — flights from Athens to Santorini
sources.claim: Aegean's Athens-Santorini one-way fares start at €50, August 2026 range about €50-106.

sources.title: Sky Express — flights from Athens to Santorini
sources.claim: Sky Express Athens-Santorini one-way fares start at €44, August 2026 dates €52-99.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — SeaJets WorldChampion Jet
sources.claim: WorldChampion Jet does Piraeus-Mykonos in about 2.5-3 hours and Piraeus-Santorini in about 5.5 hours.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — Santorini airport
sources.claim: JTR advises 1 hour before a carry-on flight, 2+ with bags; only ~40 taxis serve the island at €30-45.

sources.title: Rick Steves forum — island ferries and motion sickness
sources.claim: Catamarans and hydrofoils provoke far more motion sickness than large conventional ferries.

sources.title: Public Transport Guide — Athens metro ticket prices 2026
sources.claim: The 2026 airport metro fare is €9 one-way / €16 return; €1.20 city tickets are not valid.

sources.title: Athens Tourism — Athens to Greek islands ferry guide
sources.claim: Piraeus has 12 gates (E1-E12) and wants 60-90 minutes of buffer.
